## The problem

Build an alarm controller with DISARMED, ARMING, ARMED, ALARM, and SILENCED
states. A switch provides the input; safe indicator outputs show the state. Any
relay, lamp, or horn is controlled by an approved driver rather than a GPIO pin.

## Program design

The program separates state logic from hardware access. This permits tests on a
regular Linux computer before connecting GPIO. Insert a state-transition table
and explain what happens for valid, repeated, or unexpected inputs.

## Test evidence

| Test sequence | Expected final state | Synthetic result | Log produced? |
|---|---|---|---|
| arm, wait | ARMED | ARMED | yes |
| arm, trigger | ALARM | ALARM | yes |
| trigger while disarmed | DISARMED | DISARMED | yes |
| alarm, silence | SILENCED | SILENCED | yes |

## Mistake and revision

The first loop treated a held button as many presses. I revised the input logic
to respond once per deliberate change and added a test for a switch that remains
closed.

## Conclusion

Passing software tests supports the state logic; it does not prove the external
circuit is safe or correctly wired. Hardware verification requires power-off
inspection, voltage checks, and staged output testing.
